mainTopic: Which מצוות of בני נח come from which פסוק, which ones carry the death penalty for a בן נח, and what the ברייתא means by acts 'similar to' robbery, יפת תואר and bloodshed
overview: The גמרא finishes listing the sources of דבי מנשה for the מצוות of בני נח, such as עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות, שפיכות דמים, גזל, אבר מן החי, סירוס and כלאים. After each one it shows how the other view reads the same פסוק for a different lesson. Next it asks for which מצוות a בן נח is put to death. רב יוסף says three. רב ששת attacks that list and says four, adding עבודה זרה, and רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that for a בן נח 'their warning is their death.' רב's students say a בן נח is killed for all seven. The גמרא tests that view against a ברייתא about robbery that uses the words 'forbidden' and 'permitted.' It then asks what the ברייתא means by acts 'similar to robbery.' After two answers are rejected, it settles on withholding a worker's wages. It also explains 'similar to יפת תואר' as a maidservant set aside for a slave. Finally it notes that no 'similar to bloodshed' case is taught, and אביי links such a case to רבי יונתן בן שאול, whose teaching continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The word 'corruption' points to idolatry and forbidden relations
steps.stepSummary: דבי מנשה learns the ban on עבודה זרה and גילוי עריות for בני נח from the פסוק 'the earth was corrupt before God,' using a rule from דבי רבי ישמעאל that 'corruption' always means these two sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And the earth was corrupt before God.' And the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: anywhere the Torah uses the word 'corruption,' it means only sexual sin and idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source that דבי מנשה uses to show that בני נח were forbidden in עבודה זרה and גילוי עריות. It quotes a פסוק from the generation of the flood and a general rule about the word 'corruption.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק itself only says the world was 'corrupt.' The rule from דבי רבי ישמעאל defines that word as meaning עבודה זרה and גילוי עריות. Since the generation of the flood was punished for this, these sins must have been forbidden to them.

keyTerms.meaning: corruption; the Torah's word that hints at serious sin
a teaching from the study house of רבי ישמעאל

steps.confusionAlert: This line is a continuation. The teaching of דבי מנשה started before this point, so 'as it is written' is giving the source for עבודה זרה and גילוי עריות, which were named just before.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And the earth was corrupt before God."
phrases.notes: בראשית 6:11

phrases.english: And the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Anywhere that "corruption" is stated,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא דְּבַר עֶרְוָה וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
phrases.english: it means nothing other than sexual immorality and idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַתִּשָּׁחֵת הָאָרֶץ לִפְנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the teaching of דבי מנשה that began before this section, giving its first source.
steps.raayaObject: That בני נח are forbidden in עבודה זרה and גילוי עריות
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 6:11 together with the rule of דבי רבי ישמעאל about the word השחתה

steps.title: Proof that 'corruption' means each of these two sins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up the rule of דבי רבי ישמעאל with one פסוק showing 'corruption' means sexual sin and another showing it means idol worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sexual sin, as it says: 'For all flesh had corrupted its way.' Idol worship, as it is written: 'Lest you act corruptly and make (a carved image).'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the rule from the last step by showing two פסוקים where the word 'corruption' is used for each sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each sin gets its own proof. In בראשית, 'corrupted its way' is tied to sexual sin. In דברים, 'act corruptly' is directly tied to making an idol.

keyTerms.meaning: its way; here read as hinting at relations

phrases.english: Sexual immorality: as it is stated:
"For all flesh had corrupted its way."
phrases.notes: בראשית 6:12. Here 'way' is read as hinting at intimate relations.

phrases.english: Idol worship: as it is written:
"Lest you act corruptly and make, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 4:16. The פסוק goes on to say 'a carved image.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר עֶרְוָה – שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the general rule quoted in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That the word השחתה means גילוי עריות and עבודה זרה

steps.title: The other view reads the flood verse as only describing behavior
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the other view does with 'the earth was corrupt,' and answers that for them it just describes how that generation acted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other view? (For them, the פסוק) is just revealing their behavior.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the other view, which learns the מצוות of בני נח from a different source, reads this פסוק. It answers right away: the פסוק only tells us how the people behaved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other view does not need this פסוק as a source for a prohibition. So it reads it as a description of how bad the generation of the flood was, not as the origin of a law.

keyTerms.meaning: and the other one? (how does the other view read this?)

phrases.english: And the other view?
phrases.notes: The other opinion, mentioned earlier, which learns these מצוות from a different פסוק.

phrases.english: It is revealing their behavior.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the opposing view reads the פסוק used in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the other view learns from 'ותשחת הארץ'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It only describes the behavior of the generation of the flood.

steps.title: Source for the ban on murder
steps.stepSummary: דבי מנשה learns the ban on שפיכות דמים for בני נח from 'One who sheds the blood of man.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Bloodshed, as it is written: 'One who sheds the blood of man (by man his blood shall be shed).'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the list of דבי מנשה and gives the source for the ban on murder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק was said to נח and his sons after the flood. It punishes one who kills, which shows that killing is forbidden to all people.

keyTerms.meaning: one who sheds the blood of a person

phrases.english: Bloodshed, as it is written:
"One who sheds the blood of man, etc."
phrases.notes: בראשית 9:6

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the list of דבי מנשה after the side question in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That בני נח are forbidden to murder

steps.title: The other view reads the murder verse as giving the punishment
steps.stepSummary: The other view uses 'One who sheds the blood of man' to teach the death penalty for בני נח, not the ban itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other view? (For them, the פסוק) is revealing their death penalty.
steps.whatsHappening: Again the גמרא asks how the other view reads this פסוק. It answers that the פסוק tells us what punishment a בן נח gets for murder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other view already knows murder is forbidden from its own source. So it reads this פסוק as adding new information: the type of death penalty, not the prohibition.

phrases.english: And the other view?
It is revealing their death penalty.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ? קְטָלַיְיהוּ הוּא דְּקָמְגַלֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 3, now for the murder פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the other view learns from 'שופך דם האדם'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It teaches the death penalty for a בן נח who murders.

steps.title: Source for the ban on robbery
steps.stepSummary: דבי מנשה learns the ban on גזל from 'like the green herbs I have given you everything,' as explained by רבי לוי: like wild grass, not like a private garden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Robbery, as it is written: 'Like the green herbs I have given you everything.' And רבי לוי said: like wild green herbs, and not like the vegetables of a garden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source of דבי מנשה for the ban on robbery. רבי לוי explains how the פסוק hints at it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wild grass belongs to no one, so anyone may take it. By saying 'like wild grass' and not 'like a garden,' the פסוק hints that what belongs to someone else may not be taken. That is the ban on גזל.

keyTerms.meaning: robbery, taking what belongs to someone else
green wild herbs that grow on their own
garden vegetables that have an owner
an אמורא who explains the פסוק

phrases.english: Robbery, as it is written:
"Like the green herbs I have given you everything."
phrases.notes: בראשית 9:3

phrases.english: And Rabbi Levi said:
Like green wild herbs, and not like garden vegetables.
phrases.notes: Wild herbs are free for anyone to take; a garden belongs to its owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּזֵל, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the list of דבי מנשה after the side question in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That בני נח are forbidden to rob
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 9:3 as explained by רבי לוי

steps.title: The other view reads the herbs verse as allowing meat
steps.stepSummary: The other view says 'like the green herbs I have given you everything' comes to permit eating meat, not to forbid robbery.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other view? That פסוק comes to permit meat.
steps.whatsHappening: For the third time the גמרא asks how the other view reads the פסוק. It answers that the פסוק is telling נח he may now eat meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the flood people ate only plants. This פסוק says that now animals are given 'just like plants' were. So the other view uses it to permit meat, not as a source for the ban on robbery.
steps.whatToRemember: The pattern in this section is that דבי מנשה finds a separate פסוק for each מצוה of בני נח. Each time, the other view reads that same פסוק as teaching something else: behavior, punishment, or permission to eat meat.

phrases.english: And the other view?
That verse comes to permit meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ? הָהוּא לְמִישְׁרֵי בָּשָׂר הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as steps 3 and 5, now for the robbery פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the other view learns from 'כירק עשב נתתי לכם את כל'

steps.title: Source for the ban on a limb from a living animal
steps.stepSummary: דבי מנשה learns the ban on אבר מן החי for בני נח from 'Only flesh with its life, its blood, you shall not eat.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The ban on eating a limb from a living animal comes from the פסוק 'Only flesh with its life, its blood, you shall not eat.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives דבי מנשה's source for the next item on his list: the ban on eating a limb cut from a living animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'flesh with its life' are read as meat taken while the animal is still alive. So the פסוק becomes a ban on אבר מן החי for all people, not only for Jews.

keyTerms.meaning: A limb cut from an animal while it is still alive
With its life, meaning while the animal is still alive

phrases.english: A limb from a living animal, as it is written:
"Only flesh with its life, its blood, you shall not eat."
phrases.notes: בראשית 9:4

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵבֶר מִן הַחַי, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of דבי מנשה's sources, after גזל.
steps.raayaObject: The ban on אבר מן החי for בני נח
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 9:4, 'אך בשר בנפשו דמו לא תאכלו'

steps.title: The other view uses the verse to permit a limb from living creeping creatures
steps.stepSummary: The other view says the פסוק comes to permit a limb from living שרצים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other view? That פסוק comes to permit creeping creatures.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the other view does with this פסוק, and answers that it teaches a leniency about שרצים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other view does not read the פסוק as a new ban. It reads it as teaching that a limb from a living שרץ is permitted. So the same words are used for a different lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one? How does the other view use this פסוק?

phrases.english: And the other view?
That verse comes to permit creeping creatures.
phrases.notes: So a limb taken from a living שרץ is not forbidden to a בן נח.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ? הָהוּא לְמִישְׁרֵי שְׁרָצִים הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other view's reading of the פסוק brought in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the other view learn from 'אך בשר בנפשו'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It permits a limb from living שרצים; it is not a ban.

steps.title: Source for the ban on castration
steps.stepSummary: דבי מנשה learns the ban on סירוס from 'swarm in the earth and multiply in it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The ban on castration comes from the פסוק 'Swarm in the earth and multiply in it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives דבי מנשה's source for the ban on castrating, meaning making a creature unable to have young.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק tells living things to multiply. דבי מנשה reads this as a command, so making a creature unable to reproduce goes against it.

keyTerms.meaning: Castration, making a creature unable to reproduce

phrases.english: Castration, as it is written:
"Swarm in the earth and multiply in it."
phrases.notes: בראשית 9:7

steps.triggerLanguage: סֵירוּס, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item on דבי מנשה's list.
steps.raayaObject: The ban on סירוס for בני נח

steps.title: The other view reads it as only a blessing
steps.stepSummary: The other view says 'swarm and multiply' is only a blessing, not a command.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other view? It is just a blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the other view reads this פסוק, and answers that it is only a ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the words are a blessing ('may you multiply'), there is no command in them. Without a command, there is no source for a ban on סירוס.

phrases.english: And the other view?
It is merely a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ? לִבְרָכָה בְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other view's reading of the פסוק in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the other view do with 'שרצו בארץ ורבו בה'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a blessing, not a מצוה.

steps.title: Source for the ban on mixing species
steps.stepSummary: דבי מנשה learns the ban on כלאים from 'of the fowl after their kind.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The ban on mixing species comes from the פסוק 'Of the fowl after their kind.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives דבי מנשה's source for כלאים, the ban on crossbreeding different species.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ark, each kind of animal was kept 'after its kind.' דבי מנשה reads this as a rule that species must stay separate, so crossbreeding is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: After its kind, each by its own species

phrases.english: Mixing species, as it is written:
"Of the fowl after their kind."
phrases.notes: בראשית 6:20, about the animals going into the ark.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּלְאַיִם, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Last item on דבי מנשה's list.
steps.raayaObject: The ban on כלאים for בני נח

steps.title: The other view says it was only for companionship
steps.stepSummary: The other view says the animals were kept by species only so they would have company, not because of a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other view? That was merely for companionship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the other view reads this פסוק, and answers that keeping each kind together was just for company.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other view sees the פסוק as describing a practical arrangement in the ark. It is not a law. So there is no source for a ban on כלאים for בני נח.

keyTerms.meaning: For companionship, so they would have company

steps.whatToRemember: For each extra item on דבי מנשה's list (אבר מן החי, סירוס, כלאים), the other view keeps the פסוק but gives it a different job: a leniency, a blessing, or a practical detail. None of them becomes a ban.

phrases.english: And the other view?
That was merely for companionship.
phrases.notes: Each kind was kept together in the ark so the animals would be comfortable with their own kind.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ? הָהוּא לְצַוְתָּא בְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other view's reading of the פסוק in step 12, closing the list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the other view do with 'מהעוף למינהו'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It was just for companionship in the ark, not a מצוה.

steps.title: A בן נח is executed for only three מצוות
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף reports that the study hall teaches that a בן נח is put to death for three מצוות: גילוי עריות, שפיכות דמים, and ברכת השם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: They say in the study hall that a בן נח is executed for three מצוות (memory aid: גשר): for forbidden relations, for bloodshed, and for cursing God's name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new point. רב יוסף says only three of the מצוות of בני נח carry the death penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the topic was which מצוות a בן נח has. Now רב יוסף narrows the death penalty to just three of them. Notice that עבודה זרה is not on this list, even though it is one of the מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'blessing the Name'; a polite way of saying cursing God

steps.confusionAlert: 'ברכת השם' does not mean blessing God. It is a polite way of saying cursing God's name.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אָמְרִי בֵּי רַב,
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: They say in the study hall,

phrases.aramaic: עַל שָׁלֹשׁ מִצְוֹת בֶּן נֹחַ נֶהֱרָג
phrases.english: for three מצוות a descendant of Noah is executed
(the memory aid is גשר):
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out these words in round brackets. The memory aid works like this: ג for גילוי, ש for שפיכות, and ר for ברכת.

phrases.english: for forbidden sexual relations,
and for bloodshed,
and for 'blessing' the Name.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אָמְרִי בֵּי רַב, עַל שָׁלֹשׁ מִצְוֹת בֶּן נֹחַ נֶהֱרָג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the sources of the מצוות to which ones carry the death penalty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בן נח is executed only for גילוי עריות, שפיכות דמים, and ברכת השם.

steps.title: רב ששת asks for the source of the other two death penalties
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת accepts that a בן נח is killed for שפיכות דמים because a פסוק says so, but asks where we learn death for the other items on רב יוסף's list.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת objects: Bloodshed makes sense, since the Torah says 'whoever sheds the blood of man, by man his blood shall be shed.' But where do we learn the death penalty for the others?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת is challenging רב יוסף's list of three. He agrees with one item and demands a source for the other two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שפיכות דמים there is a clear פסוק giving a בן נח the death penalty. For גילוי עריות and ברכת השם there is no such obvious פסוק. This opens an attack that the next step will sharpen.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it; an attack on a statement
It makes sense / granted (accepting one part before challenging another)
From where do they know it? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet objects to this:
Granted, bloodshed works,
as it is written: 'One who sheds the blood of man, etc.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 9:6. The rest of the פסוק says 'by man his blood shall be shed', which is the death penalty.

phrases.english: But those others, where do they learn them from?
phrases.notes: 'Those others' are גילוי עריות and ברכת השם from רב יוסף's list.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's report of three capital מצוות for a בן נח.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's list of three מצוות for which a בן נח is killed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only שפיכות דמים has a clear פסוק giving a death penalty. The other two items lack an obvious source.

steps.title: Any possible source would prove too much
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת shows that both possible sources for the other two penalties fail. Learning from שפיכות דמים would include all seven מצוות, and learning from 'איש איש' would also include עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you learn them from bloodshed, then the death penalty should apply to all of the מצוות. If you include them because of the words 'איש איש', then עבודה זרה is also included by 'איש איש'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת tests two possible sources for the death penalty and shows that neither one fits a list of exactly three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: compare everything to שפיכות דמים. Nothing would limit that comparison, so all seven מצוות of a בן נח would carry death. Option two: the Torah uses 'איש איש' for ברכת השם and for עריות, and that phrase includes non-Jews. But 'איש איש' also appears with עבודה זרה, so it would have to be on the list too.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns, derives (one law from another)
It was included (by an extra word in the פסוק)
'Any man', a doubled word read as including non-Jews

steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת is not saying all seven מצוות carry death. He is showing that the first possible source would lead there, which is why it cannot be the right source.

phrases.english: If he learns it from bloodshed,
then even all of them too.
phrases.notes: All seven מצוות of a בן נח, not just these three.

phrases.english: If it is because they are included from 'איש איש',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:15 for ברכת השם and ויקרא 18:6 for עריות.

phrases.english: then idol worship too
is included from 'איש איש'.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:2.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי גָּמַר מִשְּׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים, אֲפִילּוּ כּוּלְּהוּ נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sharpens the question of step 15 by ruling out both possible sources.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that exactly three מצוות carry death for a בן נח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma: one source proves all seven, and the other proves four, including עבודה זרה. Neither gives exactly three.

steps.title: רב ששת's version: four מצוות
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת gives a different version of the study-hall teaching: a בן נח is put to death for four מצוות, adding עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב ששת said: In the study hall they say that a בן נח is put to death for four מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the list of three cannot stand, רב ששת corrects the report of what the study hall taught. The list has four items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows from the 'איש איש' source in step 16. That phrase covers ברכת השם, עריות, and עבודה זרה. Together with שפיכות דמים, that makes four.

keyTerms.meaning: The study hall, the house of learning
A descendant of נח, a non-Jew

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next challenge. Putting עבודה זרה on the death list now has to be squared with a ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Sheshet said:
They say in the study hall:

phrases.aramaic: עַל אַרְבַּע מִצְוֹת בֶּן נֹחַ נֶהֱרָג.
phrases.english: For four מצוות a בן נח is put to death.
phrases.notes: The three from before plus עבודה זרה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: אָמְרִי בֵּי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יוסף's version, which step 16 disproved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בן נח is put to death for four מצוות: שפיכות דמים, גילוי עריות, ברכת השם, and עבודה זרה.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to give only a warning for עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ששת from a ברייתא that says a בן נח is 'warned' about forms of עבודה זרה. This implies a prohibition with no death penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a בן נח really killed for עבודה זרה? But a ברייתא teaches: In עבודה זרה, the acts for which a Jewish court executes, a בן נח is warned about them. That means a warning, yes, but death, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב ששת's addition of עבודה זרה by quoting a ברייתא that seems to give a בן נח only a prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the word 'מוזהר', meaning 'is warned'. It does not say 'is killed'. The גמרא reads this as meaning a בן נח has the prohibition but not the death penalty, which goes against רב ששת.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (introducing a challenge)

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בֶּן נֹחַ נֶהֱרָג?
phrases.english: And is a בן נח put to death for idol worship?
But it was taught: Regarding idol worship,
the acts for which a Jewish court
executes over them,
a בן נח is warned about them.
A warning, yes; death, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בֶּן נֹחַ נֶהֱרָג? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's list of four in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's inclusion of עבודה זרה as a capital crime for a בן נח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says only 'מוזהר' (warned), which implies a prohibition without a death penalty.

steps.title: For a בן נח, the warning is the death penalty
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that for a בן נח, any אזהרה automatically carries death. So the ברייתא's word 'warned' already means he is put to death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Their warning is their death.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק defends רב ששת by reinterpreting the word 'warned' in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a Jew, a prohibition and its punishment are separate questions, so 'warned' would not mean 'executed'. For a בן נח there is no separate list of punishments: whatever he is warned about carries death. So the ברייתא does not contradict רב ששת.

keyTerms.meaning: Their warning is itself their death penalty

steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת holds that a בן נח is killed for four מצוות, including עבודה זרה. The ברייתא saying he is only 'warned' is not a problem, because for a בן נח the warning itself means death.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'their warning is their death' as 'they get no punishment'. It means the opposite: for a בן נח, being forbidden is enough to make the act a capital crime.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Their warning – that is their death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: אַזְהָרָה שֶׁלָּהֶן זוֹ הִיא מִיתָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 and keeps רב ששת's list of four.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a term: 'warned' for a בן נח already includes death.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מוזהר' means a prohibition with no death penalty, as it would for a Jew.
steps.terutzMaskana: For a בן נח, any אזהרה carries death, so עבודה זרה is a capital crime for him.

steps.title: רב's students: a בן נח is killed for all seven מצוות
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא, רב יהודה and all of רב's students hold that a בן נח is put to death for breaking any of his seven מצוות. The תורה wrote the death penalty for one of them, and the same applies to all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, רב יהודה and all of רב's students say: a בן נח is killed for any of the seven מצוות. The תורה revealed it about one, and the same is true for all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third, wider opinion: death for all seven מצוות, not just three or four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת had argued that learning from שפיכות דמים would cover all seven מצוות, and he saw that as a problem. רב's students accept exactly that: since the תורה gave death for one מצוה, all seven get the same punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: The seven commandments given to all of mankind
The Merciful One (the תורה) revealed it in one case

phrases.english: Rav Huna and Rav Yehuda
and all the students of Rav say:

phrases.aramaic: עַל שֶׁבַע מִצְוֹת בֶּן נֹחַ נֶהֱרָג.
phrases.english: For seven מצוות a descendant of Noah is killed.
The Merciful One revealed it with one,
phrases.notes: The 'one' is murder, where the פסוק clearly gives death, as we saw in step 15.

phrases.english: and the same is true for all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא וְרַב יְהוּדָה וְכוּלְּהוּ תַּלְמִידֵי דְּרַב אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third version of the teaching, after רב יוסף's three and רב ששת's four. It accepts the wide reading that רב ששת rejected in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בן נח is put to death for breaking any of the seven מצוות. The rule is learned from שפיכות דמים and applied to all of them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the widest view. The rest of the sugya tests it, starting with robbery.

steps.title: Challenge: a ברייתא calls robbery only 'forbidden' for a בן נח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a בן נח is really killed for robbery. A ברייתא says robbery and similar acts are 'forbidden' (אסור) for a gentile. If he were killed for them, it should have said 'liable' (חייב).
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a בן נח really killed for robbery? A ברייתא teaches: stealing, robbing, a יפת תואר and similar acts are forbidden from gentile to gentile and from gentile to Jew, and permitted from Jew to gentile. If he were killed, it should say 'liable'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's students using a ברייתא about robbery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the word אסור, 'forbidden'. That sounds like a ban with no death penalty. If robbery carried death, the natural word would be חייב, 'liable'. So robbery seems to be an exception to 'all seven'.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (opening a challenge)

phrases.english: And for robbery, is a descendant of Noah killed?
But it was taught: Regarding robbery,
one who stole or robbed,
and likewise a woman captured in war,
and likewise anything similar to them –
a gentile to a gentile, or a gentile to a Jew, is forbidden,
and a Jew to a gentile is permitted.
And if it is so, let it teach 'liable'!
phrases.notes: 'If it is so' means: if a בן נח really were killed for robbery.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל הַגָּזֵל בֶּן נֹחַ נֶהֱרָג? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the opinion of רב's students from step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a בן נח is killed for all seven מצוות, including robbery.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא uses אסור rather than חייב for a gentile who robs. That suggests a ban without the death penalty.

steps.title: The ברייתא said 'forbidden' only to match 'permitted'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא wanted to say that a Jew taking from a gentile is מותר. To match that word, it said אסור in the first part. So the wording does not prove there is no death penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the ברייתא wanted to teach in the later part that a Jew to a gentile is permitted, it taught 'forbidden' in the first part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב's students by explaining the ברייתא's choice of words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opposite of חייב is פטור, 'exempt'. Saying a Jew is פטור could sound like the act is still forbidden for him, just not punished. The ברייתא wanted to say clearly that it is מותר, so it used the matching word אסור for the gentile.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of a teaching
The first part of a teaching

phrases.english: Because he wanted to teach in the later clause:
'a Jew to a gentile is permitted,'
he taught in the first clause: 'forbidden.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָבָעֵי לְמִיתְנֵי סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the word choice as style: the ברייתא picked אסור to match מותר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word אסור shows that robbery carries no death for a בן נח.
steps.terutzMaskana: אסור was chosen to pair with מותר, so it says nothing against the death penalty.

steps.title: Pushback: the same ברייתא does say 'liable' and 'exempt' for murder
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer. In its first part, about murder, the same ברייתא says a gentile is חייב and a Jew is פטור. So wherever there is a death penalty, this ברייתא says so.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wherever there is liability, it does teach it. In the first part it teaches: for murder, a gentile to a gentile or a gentile to a Jew is liable, and a Jew to a gentile is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of step 22 by pointing to an earlier line of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 said the ברייתא avoided חייב and פטור for style reasons. But the murder clause uses exactly that pair. So in the robbery clause, the change to אסור and מותר seems to mean something real: no death penalty for robbery.
steps.confusionAlert: Here פטור for a Jew who kills a gentile means only that a human court does not execute him. It does not mean the act is allowed.

phrases.english: But wherever
there is liability,
it does teach it,
as it teaches in the first clause: regarding bloodshed –
a gentile to a gentile, or a gentile to a Jew, is liable,
a Jew to a gentile is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּאִית לֵיהּ חִיּוּבָא מִיתְנָא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 22 and brings back the challenge of step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 22 that the ברייתא avoided חייב and פטור only for style.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same ברייתא uses חייב and פטור for murder. So its use of אסור for robbery seems deliberate, showing there is no death penalty for robbery.

steps.title: Murder could not be described as forbidden versus permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the murder case says חייב and פטור. The pair אסור and מותר would wrongly suggest that a Jew may kill a gentile, and a ברייתא shows that this is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the murder case, how else could the ברייתא say it? Should it say 'forbidden' and 'permitted'? But a ברייתא teaches that a gentile and shepherds of small animals are neither raised out of a pit nor lowered into one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 23. The murder case could not use the words 'forbidden' and 'permitted,' because killing a gentile is not actually permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 23 the challenge was: in murder the ברייתא says חייב, so why not in robbery too? The answer is that in murder, writing מותר for the Jew would be false, since the rule is only that one does not rescue and does not kill. In robbery, taking from a gentile really is מותר, so the ברייתא wrote אסור to match it. That brings back the answer from step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: How should he teach it? This asks what other wording was possible.
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא?
Shepherds of small animals like sheep and goats. In that time they were known for grazing on other people's land.
We do not raise them out of a pit and we do not lower them into one. We don't rescue them, but we don't kill them either.

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא does not permit killing a gentile. 'Not lowering' means you may not cause his death. That is exactly why the murder case could not use the word מותר.

phrases.english: There, how should he teach it?
Should he teach 'forbidden' and 'permitted'?
But isn't it taught:
A gentile, and shepherds of small livestock —
we do not raise them up and we do not lower them down.
phrases.notes: Raising them out of a pit they fell into, or lowering them into one.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם, הֵיכִי לִיתְנֵי? לִיתְנֵי ״אָסוּר״ וּ״מוּתָּר״?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 23 and restores the wording explanation from step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains a difference in wording between the two cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the murder case says חייב, the robbery case should also say חייב if there were a death penalty.
steps.terutzMaskana: The murder case had to say חייב and פטור, because killing a gentile is not מותר. In robbery, מותר is true for the Jew, so the ברייתא wrote אסור to match.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gentile and shepherds of small livestock are not rescued from a pit, but they may not be pushed into one.

steps.title: What counts as 'similar to robbery'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means by acts that are 'similar to robbery.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And acts similar to robbery.' What is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a phrase in the ברייתא about robbery. It asks what acts are 'similar to robbery.' This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary גזל is already covered by the word 'robbery.' So the extra words must add some borderline case. The גמרא wants to know which case that is.

phrases.english: 'Similar to it' in robbery, what is it?
phrases.notes: These words come from the ברייתא in step 21: 'robbery and things similar to it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ בְּגָזֵל, מַאי הִיא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the death-penalty discussion and clarifies a phrase in the same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case is included by the words 'similar to robbery'?

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב: a worker in a vineyard
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב says the phrase refers to a worker who eats from the vineyard he works in.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: It is only needed for a worker in a vineyard.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב gives the first answer. 'Similar to robbery' means a worker eating grapes in the vineyard where he works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A worker eating his employer's fruit looks like it might be allowed. It also looks like it might be taking. רב אחא בר יעקב suggests the ברייתא forbids this for a gentile worker.

keyTerms.meaning: It was only needed for. This points to the one case the words come to teach.
A hired worker in a vineyard
An אמורא who offers the first explanation

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov said:
It is needed only for a laborer in a vineyard.
phrases.notes: The worker eating the fruit while he works.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְפוֹעֵל בַּכֶּרֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A worker eating from the vineyard he works in.

steps.title: The vineyard worker is either allowed or simply stealing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the vineyard case does not work. If the worker eats while finishing the work, it is permitted. If not, it is plain robbery.
steps.simpleTranslation: A worker in a vineyard, when? If he eats at the time the work is being finished, it is permitted. If not at that time, it is full robbery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אחא בר יעקב. Either way, the vineyard case is not an in-between case that needs the words 'similar to robbery.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא splits the case into two possibilities. At the time of finishing the work, eating is allowed, so there is nothing to forbid. At any other time, it is plain גזל, which the word 'robbery' already covers. Either way, the case does not explain the extra words.

keyTerms.meaning: The finishing of the work, such as the harvest

phrases.english: A laborer in a vineyard — when?
If at the time of the completion of the work —
it is permitted,
phrases.notes: See דברים 23:25.

phrases.english: if it is not at the time of the completion of the work —
it is full-fledged robbery.

steps.triggerLanguage: פּוֹעֵל בַּכֶּרֶם אֵימַת?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of רב אחא בר יעקב in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's claim that 'similar to robbery' means the vineyard worker
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Either way the case fails. If it is permitted, there is nothing to forbid. If it is plain robbery, the word 'robbery' already covers it.

steps.title: רב פפא: stealing less than a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a new answer. 'Similar to robbery' means taking something worth less than a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: It is only needed for less than the value of a פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא replaces the rejected answer. The phrase teaches that taking a tiny amount, less than a פרוטה, is also forbidden for a gentile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Less than a פרוטה is too small to count as real money in many areas of הלכה. That makes it a true in-between case. The ברייתא's extra words teach that a בן נח may not take even that.

keyTerms.meaning: The smallest coin that counts as value in halacha
Less than the worth of a פרוטה
An אמורא who offers the second explanation

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְפָחוֹת מִשָּׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה.
phrases.english: It is needed only for less than the value of a peruta.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since step 27 rejected the vineyard answer, רב פפא offers a different case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Taking something worth less than a פרוטה.

steps.title: But people forgive such small amounts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא. Why would it be forbidden for a gentile to take less than a פרוטה from a Jew, when a Jew forgives such a small loss?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it is forbidden for a gentile to take from a Jew? But a Jew is someone who forgives this!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא's answer. If the owner will surely forgive so small a loss, why is it considered taking at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says it is אסור for a gentile to rob a Jew. If the case is less than a פרוטה, the owner does not really mind losing it. So there seems to be no wrong done.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who forgives. A person likely to let it go.

phrases.english: If so, a gentile with a Jew is forbidden?
But he is one who forgives!
phrases.notes: 'He' is the Jewish owner, who would not care about something worth so little.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, גּוֹי בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל אָסוּר? הָא בַּר מְחִילָה הוּא!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's answer from step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that the ברייתא forbids taking less than a פרוטה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the owner forgives such a tiny loss, no wrong seems to be done. So why would the ברייתא forbid it?

steps.title: He is still upset at the moment it is taken
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that even if the owner forgives later, he still feels upset at the moment it is taken. So the act is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted that afterward he forgives him. But doesn't he feel distress at that moment?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב פפא. The owner's later forgiveness does not erase the pain he felt when the item was taken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge looked at what happens later, when the owner lets it go. The answer looks at the moment of the act, when the owner is hurt, so a gentile taking less than a פרוטה from a Jew is forbidden. This defends רב פפא for now, but the next step raises a new problem with his answer.
steps.whatToRemember: The answer here saves רב פפא only for a gentile taking from a Jew: the owner is hurt at the moment it is taken, even if he forgives later. The next step shows his answer still fails between two gentiles.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the wrong in robbery is judged at the moment of the act, not by whether the owner lets it go afterward.

phrases.english: Granted that afterward he forgives him,
does he not have distress at the time?

steps.triggerLanguage: נְהִי דְּבָתַר הָכִי מָחֵיל לֵיהּ, צַעֲרָא בְּשַׁעְתֵּיהּ מִי לֵית לֵיהּ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29 and keeps רב פפא's explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the focus to the moment of the act
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the owner forgives a tiny loss, taking less than a פרוטה is no wrong at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The owner is hurt at the moment it is taken, so the act is forbidden even though he forgives later.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For now, רב פפא's reading stands: taking less than a פרוטה from a Jew is forbidden for a בן נח, because the owner is hurt at the moment it is taken. Step 31 then rejects this reading, and step 32 gives the final answer.

steps.title: The less-than-a-coin answer fails for a gentile robbing a gentile
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא again. Between two gentiles, nobody forgives, so even taking less than a פרוטה is real robbery, not just 'similar to robbery'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a gentile robbing a gentile, the 'similar' case there? Gentiles do not forgive small losses, so taking even a tiny amount is full robbery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with רב פפא's answer. Between two gentiles, taking less than a פרוטה is plain robbery, so it cannot be the 'similar to robbery' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 30, the גמרא said a Jew forgives a tiny loss later but is still upset when it is taken. Gentiles, though, are not people who forgive at all. So when one gentile takes a tiny amount from another, it is simply robbery, and רב פפא's idea does not explain the 'similar' category.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Similar to them': cases that resemble the main law

phrases.english: A gentile against a gentile, 'similar to them' —
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking how רב פפא's less-than-a-פרוטה idea could fit a gentile who takes from another gentile.

phrases.english: since they are not people who forgive,
it is full-fledged robbery!

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוֹי בְּגוֹי כַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהֶן, כֵּיוָן דְּלָאו בְּנֵי מְחִילָה נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Even after step 30 saved רב פפא for a gentile taking from a Jew, this step shows his answer still fails between two gentiles.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's explanation that 'similar to robbery' means taking less than a פרוטה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Gentiles never forgive, so between them a tiny taking is ordinary robbery and cannot be a separate 'similar' case.

steps.title: New answer: withholding a worker's wages
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא explains that 'similar to robbery' means holding back a hired worker's pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אחא son of רב איקא said: it is only needed for someone who holds back a worker's wages. A gentile doing this to a gentile, or a gentile doing this to a Jew, is forbidden. A Jew doing this to a gentile is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב פפא's answer was rejected, the גמרא brings a fresh answer. The 'similar to robbery' case is withholding a hired worker's wages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Withholding wages does not grab anything from the victim. It only keeps money that is owed to him. That is why it only 'resembles' robbery, yet a בן נח is still forbidden to do it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was needed only for...': introduces the specific case meant

steps.whatToRemember: The final answer for 'similar to robbery' is כובש שכר שכיר, holding back a worker's pay.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Acha son of Rav Ika said:
It was needed only
for one who withholds a hired worker's wages.
A gentile to a gentile, and a gentile to a Jew, is forbidden;
a Jew to a gentile is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְכוֹבֵשׁ שְׂכַר שָׂכִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב פפא's rejected answer with a new definition of 'similar to robbery'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the 'similar to robbery' case?

steps.title: What is 'similar to יפת תואר'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next 'similar' case and asks what resembles the captive woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case that is 'similar to יפת תואר'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to another 'similar' case from the ברייתא. It asks a question, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Robbery is now settled. The גמרא wants to know which forbidden relationship the ברייתא means by 'similar to יפת תואר'.

keyTerms.meaning: The beautiful captive woman taken in war

phrases.english: 'Similar to the beautiful captive woman' — what is it?
phrases.notes: יפת תואר is the captive woman in דברים 21:11.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּיּוֹצֵא בִּיפַת תּוֹאַר, מַאי הִיא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from robbery to the next 'similar' case in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The case that the ברייתא calls 'similar to יפת תואר'.

steps.title: רב דימי: the maidservant set aside for a slave
steps.stepSummary: A בן נח who set aside a maidservant for his slave and then had relations with her is put to death.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said in the name of רבי אלעזר from רבי חנינא: a בן נח who set aside a maidservant for his slave and then had relations with her is killed because of her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי answers the question. The 'similar' case is a maidservant whom the owner set aside for his slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She is not a full wife, yet once the owner designated her for his slave, she counts like a married woman. If the owner himself then has relations with her, he gets the death penalty.

keyTerms.meaning: A descendant of Noach, meaning a non-Jew

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
phrases.notes: He means: came from ארץ ישראל to Bavel, bringing teachings with him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Chanina:
A descendant of Noach who designated a maidservant for his slave
and had relations with her is executed on her account.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אָמַר: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A בן נח who sets aside a maidservant for his slave and then lives with her is put to death.

steps.title: No 'similar to bloodshed' case is taught
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the ברייתא gives no 'similar' case for murder.
steps.simpleTranslation: A case 'similar to bloodshed' is not taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that, unlike the other laws, murder has no 'similar' case in the ברייתא. This sets up אביי's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Robbery and forbidden relations each have a 'similar' case, but bloodshed does not. The גמרא states this fact so it can explain who might hold that there is one.

phrases.aramaic: כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ דִּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים לָא תַּנְיָא.
phrases.english: A case 'similar to' bloodshed is not taught.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ דִּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים לָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining the 'similar' cases for robbery and יפת תואר, the גמרא notes that bloodshed has none.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא lists no 'similar to bloodshed' case for בני נח.

steps.title: אביי: such a teaching would follow רבי יונתן בן שאול
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that any teaching with a 'similar to bloodshed' case follows רבי יונתן בן שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: if you find a teaching that does include it, it follows רבי יונתן בן שאול.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי responds to the observation. If someone finds a 'similar to bloodshed' teaching, its author is רבי יונתן בן שאול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי ties a possible 'similar to bloodshed' case to one specific תנא. The next step brings that תנא's ברייתא as the source.

keyTerms.meaning: That it is taught (in a ברייתא)
The תנא whose view this follows

phrases.english: Abaye said:
If you find that it is taught,
it is the view of Rabbi Yonatan ben Shaul.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן שָׁאוּל הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to step 35 by naming who would hold that a 'similar to bloodshed' case exists.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A 'similar to bloodshed' teaching would follow רבי יונתן בן שאול.

steps.title: The source: someone who could stop a pursuer by injuring a limb
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting רבי יונתן בן שאול's ברייתא about a רודף who could have been stopped without being killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי יונתן בן שאול says: if someone is chasing another person to kill him, and he could be stopped by hurting one of his limbs, but he was not stopped that way...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי יונתן בן שאול's ברייתא to back up אביי. The quote continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A רודף may be stopped, but if hurting one limb would have been enough, killing him goes too far. This case is the kind of 'similar to bloodshed' case אביי meant, and the ruling comes in the next part.

keyTerms.meaning: A pursuer chasing someone to kill him
To stop him by hurting one of his limbs
And he did not save him that way

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yonatan ben Shaul says:
One who chases after his fellow to kill him,
and it is possible to save him by injuring one of his limbs,
but he did not save him that way...

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that אביי referred to.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that a 'similar to bloodshed' case follows רבי יונתן בן שאול
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יונתן בן שאול about a רודף who could have been stopped by injuring a limb
